# 01 The corpus, and the two numbers it ratchets

## Outcome

One file says where Siren stands against Mermaid, per construct, in a form that fails when someone
regresses it — and that cannot be satisfied by a document which parses into the wrong picture.

## Why this ticket exists

Nothing in this repo fails because a valid Mermaid document does not render. That is why the gap
reached 34/39 unnoticed. It is also why the first measurement read 10/39: five cases parse cleanly
and draw the wrong thing, and a check that asks "were there diagnostics?" counts those as passes.

The corpus is the fix for both. It is the ticket everything else on this board reports to.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `packages/core/src/compat/corpus.ts` holds the cases as data — the `CompatCase` shape is in
      the board's spec. Each `source` is **valid Mermaid**; anything that is not does not belong.
- [x] Three states: `supported`, `rejected`, `silently-wrong`. The third exists because the
      measurement needs to name the dangerous class, not because it is a resting place.
- [x] `corpus.test.ts` checks each entry **against its declared status**:
      `supported` → renders, zero diagnostics, and its own `assert` passes;
      `rejected` → produces at least one error-severity diagnostic;
      `silently-wrong` → renders with zero diagnostics **and** its `assert` documents the wrong
      output it currently produces, so the entry is a statement of fact rather than a label.
- [x] **A `supported` entry with no `assert` fails the suite**, as a defect in the corpus. This is
      decision 3 in the spec, and it is the whole reason the first measurement was wrong by a
      factor of two. Do not make it a lint or a comment; make it a failure.
- [x] Two ratchet assertions against literal numbers: the count of `silently-wrong` and the count
      of `rejected`. Both literal, so moving a case forces someone to read the number.
- [x] The ratchet test's message says what the numbers mean and which direction each may move —
      `silently-wrong` toward zero, `rejected` only downward. Whoever hits it next is mid-task and
      needs to know in one line whether they broke something or made progress.
- [x] The corpus is seeded from `.dev/mermaid-compatibility-gaps.md`: all 39 flowchart cases, 13
      class-diagram cases and 15 sequence cases already measured there. **Re-measure rather than
      transcribe** — that document was written from a probe, and a transcription error would be
      invisible.
- [x] The initial counts match reality, whatever it is. If your measurement disagrees with the
      `.dev` document, **your measurement wins and you say so in your report** — the document is a
      record of one probe, not an authority.

## Status

Done (2026-09-06), commits 0d219f8 + fbcbff9. 4 slices, plus a disclosed mutation check of the
instrument itself (three mutations, two bit; the third is recorded as the hole no mechanical
check can close). 677 core tests / 22 files / 29 board, tsc clean both.

Re-measured rather than transcribed, and the measurement won twice: `.dev`'s tables total 35
rejected where running the cases gives 33, and its flowchart total of 39 enumerated 37 rows.

Reclassified on review (fbcbff9): `seq-loop` and `seq-alt-else` moved `supported` →
`silently-wrong`. Siren never draws a control-flow block's keyword, so seven kinds render
identically. Their exit is implementation, not rejection — the spec's zero-goal was amended to
name such cases rather than pretend.

## Test seam

The corpus runner, through `render()`. A silent mis-render is only visible in the result, so a
seam at the parser cannot see the class of bug this exists to catch.

## Write ownership

- `packages/core/src/compat/corpus.ts` (new)
- `packages/core/src/compat/corpus.test.ts` (new)

Nothing else. This ticket adds an instrument; it changes no behavior. If you find yourself wanting
to fix something the corpus reveals, that is a later ticket — record it as `rejected` or
`silently-wrong` and move on.
